questions.label: 4(e)
questions.text:
The initial volume of 0.17 kg of a certain gas was 0.14 m3 at a temperature of 15°C and a pressure of 1 bar. After adiabatic compression to 0.057m3, the pressure was found to be 4 bar.
Find -
i) Gas constant
ii) If ratio of specific heat is 1.407, find the value of CP and CV.
iii) Change in internal energy.
questions.marks_basis: group marks / number to attempt (not printed per sub-question)

misprint.doubt: The data are slightly inconsistent: with γ = 1.407 an adiabatic change from 0.14 m³ to 0.057 m³ would not give a final pressure of 4 bar (the end states imply γ = 1.54).
misprint.assumption: The end-state data are used as printed (T_{2} = p_{2}V_{2}/mR); this is the usual method. The alternative T_{2} from the adiabatic law would give a different ΔU.

questions.label: 5(b)
questions.text:
A closed vessel contains 0.4 m3 of steam at 10 bar and 300°C. Using following steam table -
i) Identify the quality of steam.
ii) Calculate the total enthalpy of steam
iii) Find specific volume of steam.
Take specific heat of sueperheated steam as 2.1KJ/kg K.

Absolute Pressure in bar: 10;  Temp. in °C: 179.9;  Sp. Volume (m3/kg): vf = 1.127, vg = 0.1943;  Sp. Enthalpy (kJ/kg): hf = 763.2, hg = 2778;  Sp. Entropy (kJ/kg K): sf = 2.140, sg = 6.586
questions.marks_basis: group marks / number to attempt (not printed per sub-question)

misprint.doubt: The table prints v_{f} = 1.127. The correct value is 0.001127 m³/kg (1.127 is in litres/kg, or the decimal is missing). "s_{f} = 2.140" is also not needed.
misprint.assumption: v_{f}, s_{f} and s_{g} are not needed for this question, so the answer is not affected. Only t_{s}, v_{g} and h_{g} are used.

questions.label: 6(b)
questions.text: A 100 mm thick brick wall measuring 5m × 3 m is insulated externally by cork 80 mm thick which is further protected by wood 25 mm thick. If the interior wall temperature is - 5°C and outer wall temperature is 15°C. Determine the heat transfer through the wall per hour. Take thermal conductivities of brick, cork and wood as 0.7, 0.05, 0.20 KW/m°C respectively. Also find temperature at inner surfaces.
questions.marks_basis: group marks / number to attempt (not printed per sub-question)

misprint.doubt: The thermal conductivities are printed as "0.7, 0.05, 0.20 KW/m°C". Brick, cork and wood have conductivities of 0.7, 0.05 and 0.20 W/m°C (a kilowatt value would be 1000 times too large). Also, the interior wall is colder (−5 °C) than the outer wall (15 °C), so heat flows into the room (cold store).
misprint.assumption: k is taken as 0.7, 0.05 and 0.20 W/m°C. "Temperature at inner surfaces" is taken as the temperatures of the brick–cork and cork–wood interfaces.
